intro: Discoed maps one tree: the great yew north of St Michael's Church, in a quiet corner of Radnorshire near Presteigne. Popular opinion makes it Wales's oldest yew, at 5,000 years, a figure even the guides that repeat it doubt. Measured, it is 9.68 metres round, with a second ancient yew beside it. The church was first mentioned in 1291, and a spring at the gate is now a well. Free and open.
meta_description: The Discoed Yew near Presteigne: 9.68 metres round, popularly called 5,000 years old with no proof. Free, in St Michael's churchyard.
question_meta: Discoed's oldest tree is the great yew of St Michael's churchyard, popularly called 5,000 years old, a claim nobody has proved.
question_answer: Discoed's oldest and only mapped tree is the Discoed Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) north of St Michael's Church near Presteigne in Powys. Local opinion calls it about 5,000 years old, but that figure rests on size graphs rather than evidence, and its real age is not documented.
question_context: The 5,000-year figure goes back to Allen Meredith, who estimated the ages of yews from graphs of their size, and the monument guide Wondermondo, while repeating it, says no one knows it for sure and that it is most likely not true. Several Welsh yews carry rival claims to be the oldest, and we back none of them. The measurements disagree too. The Ancient Yew Group recorded 9.68 metres at 90 centimetres in 1998; another published figure is 11.28 metres, and a 1994 gazetteer gave 22 feet. A hollow, irregular yew rarely measures the same way twice. A second ancient yew in the churchyard is 6.71 metres round, and a third notable yew stands by the lane to the car park. St Michael's is first mentioned in 1291, and a spring at the churchyard gate has become a well. Discoed has no railway or regular bus; it is about 5 km west of Presteigne. Our most recent record of the tree is not recent, so a visitor's photograph is welcome.

faq.q: How old is the Discoed Yew?
faq.a: Not documented. It is popularly called 5,000 years old, but that figure comes from size graphs, and the guides that repeat it doubt it.
The Ancient Yew Group measured 9.68 metres round in 1998; other sources give up to 11.28 metres, since a hollow yew is hard to measure the same way twice.

faq.q: How do you get to Discoed?
faq.a: There is no railway or regular bus. Discoed is about 5 km west of Presteigne, a short drive or about an hour on foot.

trees.story:
Popular opinion in this corner of Radnorshire makes the Discoed yew the oldest in Wales, some 5,000 years old. The figure goes back to Allen Meredith's graphs relating a yew's size to its age, and the monument guide Wondermondo, which repeats it, is careful to add that no one knows this for sure and that it is most likely not true. Several other Welsh yews carry rival claims. We back none of them.

The tree itself needs no exaggeration. The Ancient Yew Group measured it at 9.68 metres round, 90 centimetres up, in 1998; another figure in circulation is 11.28 metres, and a 1994 gazetteer put it at 22 feet. Yews this hollow and irregular are hard to measure the same way twice. It stands north of the small church of St Michael, first mentioned in 1291, with a second ancient yew in the same churchyard, 6.71 metres round, and a third notable one by the lane to the car park. A spring at the churchyard gate has become a well.

Nobody has dated the tree in a way that settles anything, so we give it no age. Our most recent record of it is not recent either, so if you visit St Michael's, tell us how it is doing and send a photograph.
